_comment: Short 11 in docs/CONTENT.md: the Summary of Benefits and Coverage. Linked from the app's 'What's an SBC?' box.
_injury: A stubbed toe, so hard you are sure it is broken. It gives the question the SBC answers a reason to be asked: before you go in, what will this cost?
_numbers: $30 office visit and 20% for an X-ray, the same figures as Short 3, so a viewer who has seen both recognises the plan. One figure per line.
_accuracy: 'The same layout, by law': the Affordable Care Act requires every plan to give an SBC in a uniform federal template. 'A short PDF': the template caps it at four double-sided pages.

variants.toe: You stubbed your toe so hard you are sure it is broken. Before you go in, one question. What will this cost?

body.text: Your insurance already wrote that down, in a document you have probably never opened.
It is called the Summary of Benefits and Coverage. The SBC.
Every plan has one, and by law they all use the same layout.
Find the row for what you need. An office visit, thirty dollars.
Find yours on your insurer's website, under your plan. It is a short PDF.
Then when the bill arrives, you already know what it should say.
Check yours before you dispute. Or upload them free at UseClaimRight.com.
